instructions: Take the lamb out of the fridge 2 hours before roasting. Pat it dry and trim off most of the tough white skin. Cut the garlic into slivers and break the rosemary into about 12 small pieces.
Cut about 12 small, deep slits across the meat and push a garlic sliver and a piece of rosemary into each. Rub the lamb with the oil and the pepper.
Heat the oven to 465°F. Sprinkle the lamb all over with 1 tsp of the salt, set it in a roasting pan and roast 20 minutes to form a crust.

Turn the oven down to 390°F. Roast about 50 to 60 minutes more, turning the lamb once halfway, until the meat is pink. That should be about 135°F in the thickest part, not touching the bone; a thermometer is optional. Without one, the juices should run rosy pink and the meat should spring back when pressed.
Move the lamb to a board, cover it loosely with foil and rest it at least 10 minutes.

Pour most of the fat out of the pan and set the pan over medium heat. Add the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer about 5 minutes, until reduced by about half, and season with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt or to taste.
Carve the lamb and serve with the pan sauce.
method_notes: FrenchToday's Le Gigot d'Agneau is the lead: it studs the leg with garlic, roasts hot for 20 minutes, then lowers the oven, rests the meat and makes a simple pan sauce with stock. It gives no amounts or ratings, so this is a fallback and the amounts are set for a 4 pound half leg. Snippets of Paris (5 from 2 votes) roasts with spices and a flour gravy, and Karen Bussen's version is a 7 hour braise; neither was followed. Total time is about 100 minutes because of the roast.
